- **Description:** A phrase is a palindrome if, after converting all uppercase letters into lowercase letters and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward.

**🧠 Solution Summary & Pattern Mnemonic**
- **Pattern:** Two Pointers Inward Traversal.
- **Mnemonic:** *"Meet in the middle while skipping non-alphanumerics."*
items.gotchas: • **Empty string or all spaces (`"   "`):** Pointers bypass spaces and cross over, safely returning `true`.

items.title: LeetCode 151: Reverse Words in a String — Reverse words in a string, trim whitespace, and reduce multiple spaces to a single space.
items.summary: Pattern: Regex Tokenization & Reversal. | Mnemonic: "Trim ends, split on whitespace chunks `/\s+/`, reverse, and join."
items.explanation:
- **LeetCode Link:** [LeetCode 151: Reverse Words in a String](https://leetcode.com/problems/reverse-words-in-a-string/)
- **Description:** Given an input string `s`, reverse the order of the words. Return a string of the words in reverse order concatenated by a single space.

**🧠 Solution Summary & Pattern Mnemonic**
- **Pattern:** Regex Tokenization & Reversal.
- **Mnemonic:** *"Trim ends, split on whitespace chunks `/\s+/`, reverse, and join."*
items.gotchas: • **Multiple spaces between words (`"a   good   example"`):** `/\s+/` handles arbitrary spacing cleanly.

items.title: LeetCode 283: Move Zeroes — Move all zeros to the end of an array in place while preserving order using read/write pointers vs extra array buffers.
items.summary: Pattern: Same-Direction Read/Write Pointers. | Mnemonic: "Read every element; swap non-zeros forward into the write index."
items.explanation:
- **LeetCode Link:** [LeetCode 283: Move Zeroes](https://leetcode.com/problems/move-zeroes/)
- **Description:** Given an integer array `nums`, move all `0`'s to the end of it while maintaining the relative order of the non-zero elements. You must do this **in-place** without returning anything.

**🧠 Solution Summary & Pattern Mnemonic**
- **Pattern:** Same-Direction Read/Write Pointers.
- **Mnemonic:** *"Read every element; swap non-zeros forward into the write index."*
items.gotchas: • **Do not return `nums`:** LeetCode verifies the modified array in-place. Returning a value is ignored, but allocating a copy fails memory bounds.

items.title: LeetCode 88: Merge Sorted Array — Merge two sorted arrays into nums1 in-place from back to front using 3 pointers vs array copy and sort.
items.summary: Pattern: 3-Pointer Back-to-Front In-Place Merge. | Mnemonic: "Start from the back where the empty space lives."
items.explanation:
- **LeetCode Link:** [LeetCode 88: Merge Sorted Array](https://leetcode.com/problems/merge-sorted-array/)
- **Description:** Merge two sorted integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2` into `nums1` as one sorted array in-place. `nums1` has a length of $m + n$, where the last $n$ elements are set to `0`.

**🧠 Solution Summary & Pattern Mnemonic**
- **Pattern:** 3-Pointer Back-to-Front In-Place Merge.
- **Mnemonic:** *"Start from the back where the empty space lives."*
items.gotchas: • **Loop Condition:** Only `while (p2 >= 0)` is needed. If `p2 < 0`, remaining elements in `nums1` are already in their correct sorted positions.

items.title: LeetCode 3: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters — Find the longest substring without repeating characters using dynamic sliding window with Map index jumping vs brute-force substring scanning.

items.explanation:
- **LeetCode Link:** [LeetCode 3: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters](https://leetcode.com/problems/longest-substring-without-repeating-characters/)
- **Description:** Given a string `s`, find the length of the longest substring without duplicate characters.

- **Mnemonic:** *"Expand right; on duplicate, jump left forward past its earlier position."*
items.gotchas: • **The `"abba"` Trap:** When reaching the second `'a'` at index 3, `lastSeen.get('a')` is 0. Without `Math.max(left, ...)`, `left` rewinds from 2 back to 1, corrupting window integrity.

items.title: LeetCode 20: Valid Parentheses — Check whether a string of brackets is valid using a LIFO array stack vs quadratic string replacement.
items.summary: Pattern: LIFO Stack Matching. | Mnemonic: "The most recently opened bracket must be closed first."

- **LeetCode Link:** [LeetCode 20: Valid Parentheses](https://leetcode.com/problems/valid-parentheses/)
- **Description:** Given a string `s` containing just the characters `'('`, `')'`, `'{'`, `'}'`, `'['` and `']'`, determine if the input string is valid.

items.title: LeetCode 232: Implement Queue using Stacks — Implement a FIFO queue using two LIFO array stacks with amortized O(1) operations.
items.summary: Pattern: Two Stacks (`inStack` & `outStack`) with Lazy Reversal. | Mnemonic: "Push to inStack; transfer to outStack only when outStack is empty."
items.explanation:
- **LeetCode Link:** [LeetCode 232: Implement Queue using Stacks](https://leetcode.com/problems/implement-queue-using-stacks/)
- **Description:** Implement a first in first out (FIFO) queue using only two stacks. The implemented queue should support `push`, `pop`, `peek`, and `empty`.

**🧠 Solution Summary & Pattern Mnemonic**
- **Pattern:** Two Stacks (`inStack` & `outStack`) with Lazy Reversal.
- **Mnemonic:** *"Push to inStack; transfer to outStack only when outStack is empty."*
items.gotchas: • **Amortized Analysis:** Interviewers love asking why `peek()` is $O(1)$ amortized when the `while` loop runs in $O(n)$ in the worst case. Explain that every element enters `inStack` once and `outStack` once, totaling $\le 2$ operations per element across its lifetime.
